overall: Board violated the OML by failing to publicly identify the collective bargaining units and one litigation claimant before entering executive session on July 15, 2014; other challenges were rejected or not reached. Remedy: compliance order and minutes amendment.

allegations.summary: Board entered executive session on July 15, 2014 without publicly identifying the collective bargaining unit it was negotiating with.
allegations.key_passage: we nevertheless find that it should have identified the collective bargaining unit prior to entering into executive session.

allegations.summary: Board did not publicly identify the property-damage claimant in the litigation discussed in executive session, only stating 'Property Damage Claims.'
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that including this minimal amount of information - the name of the claimant - was required, because it would have notified interested parties that this matter was being discussed behind closed doors and would not have compromised the Board's confidential discussion regarding its litigation strategy.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to adequately identify the other litigation matter (sewer plant insurance claim) before entering executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, we find that the Board did sufficiently identify the other litigation matter that it discussed in executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint questioned whether Purpose 3 (litigation strategy) was a proper basis for discussing potential litigation in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: we find that this was an appropriate discussion for executive session, as litigation was demonstrably likely.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board improperly invoked attorney/client privilege as a purpose for the executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Because we find that the executive session was proper under Purpose 3, we do not need to decide whether the attorney/client privilege would have been a valid basis for the executive session in the absence of that cited purpose.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.
Amend the July 15, 2014 open session minutes within 30 days to include the identity of the collective bargaining units and the property-damage litigation matter discussed in executive session.
remedy_passage: Additionally, we order the Board to amend its July 15, 2014 open session meeting minutes to include the identity of the collective bargaining units and the litigation matter involving property damage that it discussed in executive session.
